hunts.title: The Bog Dragon of Old Drakova
hunts.posterText: Drakovan reeve seeks proof of death — a long-shadow has been seen over the Mud Seas at dawn. Wing-mark longer than a barn. 800 TC on confirmed kill.

stages.narration: You take the Drakovan poster down off the post. The reeve confirms the bounty over a low cup of mud-beer: "Wing-mark over the marsh, two dawns running. Bring me a scale or do not come back."
stages.arbiter: "Posters in this country mean someone is desperate or someone has died," the Arbiter says. "Read the room before you sign."

stages.narration: Out on the silt flats you find the first sign — a crater of broken Aetherstone, scoured clean by something that did not land lightly.
A goat-herder's daughter saw it pass over twice. She points east, toward where the cathedral steeple breaks the water. "It roosts there now," she says. "My uncle would not go close."
You creep around the flooded approach. Bones in the silt — Reclaimer kit, mostly. The dragon has been feeding here for a while.
stages.arbiter: "It chose this place because the water hides its weight," the Arbiter says.

stages.narration: The dragon stirs. You loose an arrow at its flank and it screams once before vanishing into the mist — wounded, furious, and now hunting back.
You back-track to higher ground. The herder's daughter has set out the offering she promised — fresh meat and a torch — to draw it down to the open.
It comes for the offering. Now or never.
stages.arbiter: "Whatever you do, do not let it get airborne again," the Arbiter says.

hunts.title: The Mud Titan of the Endless Stair
hunts.posterText: True Tartarian agent in the Outskirts wants a Mud Titan put down. It is collapsing the descent to a buried capital. 600 TC and reputation with the enclave.

stages.narration: The True Tartarian agent meets you in a back alley. "Endless Stair. Halfway down, a Titan has come awake. Every shake pushes more mud into the descent. Our work cannot continue."
stages.arbiter: "They never ask quietly," the Arbiter says. "They ask only when it is bad."

stages.narration: You reach the top of the Stair. The first hundred steps are sound. Then a tremor — the railing across from you crumbles into nothing. The Titan is below, and it is moving.
You descend cautiously. Aetherstone dust comes off every wall. Six landings down, you find a Tartarian Sentinel — long dead, but with its core still loaded.
stages.arbiter: "Sentinels were built to fight what was here before us," the Arbiter says. "Their old loads may still recognise the Titan as enemy."

stages.narration: You rig the Sentinel's core to a tripwire near a chokepoint. Bait laid.
Tremor below. You see the Titan now — a hulk of moving mudstone, its shoulders scraping both walls. It is heading up.
The tripwire fires. The Sentinel core detonates against the Titan's chest. It staggers — wounded, but unkilled, and now it sees you.
The Titan charges up the steps. The wall behind you collapses, cutting off retreat. There is no second chance here.
stages.arbiter: "Finish it. Tartaria does not want a witness left," the Arbiter says.

hunts.title: The Sludge Behemoth at the Cradle of Dusk
hunts.posterText: Reclaimers Guild Speaker offers 500 TC for the head of a Behemoth that has begun crushing dive-camps near the Cradle. No fewer than four crews missing in a fortnight.

stages.narration: The Speaker reads the contract aloud. "Four crews. Eleven Reclaimers. The Behemoth has decided our dive-points are its feeding ground. End it."
The first camp is a crater. Tarpaulins ripped, equipment crushed flat. The Behemoth came up from beneath.
stages.arbiter: "It is using the silt as cover," the Arbiter says. "Watch the ground, not the horizon."

stages.narration: You set out for the second dive-point. Halfway there, the silt under your feet shifts wrong. You dive aside. The Behemoth's claw passes a hand's width from your shoulder.
The Behemoth retreats — too smart to fight on hard ground. You follow its mud-trail toward the Cradle of Dusk proper.
Inside the Cradle, ships frozen in glass watch from every side. The Behemoth has dug itself a den between two of them. The Aetheric haze here is thick — your torch will not light.
stages.arbiter: "This place keeps what it takes," the Arbiter says. "Including the Behemoth, if you fail."

stages.narration: You bait the den. A signal flare into the silt at the entrance. The Behemoth emerges.
It is wounded but not down. It backs toward open water — if it submerges, you lose it forever.
You cut the Behemoth off at the shallows. Hold ground. Finish it.
stages.arbiter: "Eleven Reclaimers," the Arbiter says. "This is the bill."

hunts.title: The Iron Titan in the Sentinel Ward
hunts.posterText: Forgotten Order requests the deactivation of an Iron Titan still patrolling a Sentinel Ward. Order scholars cannot enter their target archive. 1000 TC. Order standing.

stages.narration: Vesryn of Varakush meets you in the back of the Order safe-house. "The Iron Titan in the south Ward has not deviated from its patrol in two hundred years. We need it deactivated for a single night. Bring me its core."
stages.arbiter: "Two hundred years is a long time to compile grudges," the Arbiter says.

stages.narration: You map the Titan's patrol arc from a safe distance. Twelve-hour loop, precise to the second. Three blind spots, none long enough.
An Order scholar gives you a partial override key — Tartarian make, old and unreliable. "It will give you maybe sixty seconds of confusion. Use them."
You creep into the Ward. The air is dense with Aetheric resonance — every step the Titan takes vibrates the floor under your boots.
stages.arbiter: "Move only when it moves," the Arbiter says quietly.

stages.narration: You wedge into a service alcove as the Titan passes — close enough to touch. You can hear the Aetheric core under its plate cycling.
You burn the override. The Titan stutters for fifty-eight seconds. You move.
Mid-strike, the override fails earlier than promised. The Titan turns, sees you, and the Ward seals itself shut behind it.
No retreat. The Titan calls for backup that will not arrive in time. You have to end it before it ends you.
stages.arbiter: "This is what Reclaimers die doing," the Arbiter says. "Be better than that."

hunts.title: The Siren Queen of Zharak's Teeth
hunts.posterText: Drifters and Reclaimers alike have lost crews to the spires of Zharak's Teeth — a Mud Siren Queen leads the song. Anyone who silences her can keep what they salvage. 700 TC posted by a wandering drifter.

stages.narration: Naha hands you the poster at the wandering camp. "Drifter put this up," she says. "He won't say which crew was his. Don't ask."
Zharak's Teeth crest the water like broken jaws. Even from the shore you hear the singing — pitched too low for any human throat.
stages.arbiter: "Stuff your ears, and stuff them well," the Arbiter says. "That song has killed cleverer than you."

stages.narration: You wade in past the first spire. Drowned figures stand in the water around its base, perfectly still — Sirens, sleeping or watching, you cannot tell which.
The song shifts pitch. The standing Sirens turn their heads — not toward you. Toward something deeper. The Queen has noticed.
You find her between the two largest spires, seated on a throne of mud-glass. She is singing softly, almost lovingly, to the wreckage of the last crew that came here.
She breaks the song to address you. "You should not have come," she says, voice low and warm and utterly without anger. "But since you have — sing, or die quiet."
stages.arbiter: "She means it," the Arbiter says. "And neither option works in your favour."

stages.narration: Diplomacy bought you ten seconds. The Queen rises. The standing Sirens turn now — all of them, all toward you.
